definition: A corner is the cut, where two card edges meet. It is not the printed frame. Rounding is the arc past the measured 10–90% edge rise. The radius comes from the tip setback and from a circle fit to the silhouette. They must agree within 0.1 mm, and the upright and 180° scans must agree within 0.1 mm. A setback inside the scanner limit is a result, reported as sharp with that limit stated. The limit is the larger 10–90% rise of the two edges at that corner. Radius 0 is not published. Whitening is paper showing against the same border at mid-edge. Whitening on a border that is already paper-white is not applicable. A pale patch that is foil glare is withheld. A ding is a local notch in the cut. It is withheld when only one orientation shows it. Fraying is card-colored fiber outside the fitted cut. It is withheld when it does not rotate with the card. Length 0 is published only when both orientations are clean. A side the centering key has withheld does not grow a corner grade. TD-12 is excluded. TD-14 through TD-18 are still to come from the owner and are not measured here. Flatbed backs of TD-01 through TD-11 and Karros are a separate unapproved corner review. The two BGS slabs are reference labels only. They stay sealed, stay out of the answer key, and are an order check between corners 9.5 and corners 9. A disagreement between the two orientations, a quad that is not card-sized, or an unclear step stays withheld. Unapproved until the owner checks the overlay. No 0–10 corner score is assigned. This review does not change grading.

orderCheck.rule: Once a corner method exists, a corners 9.5 should not measure worse than a corners 9.
orderCheck.families: White-border Score and foil Momentum. This pair is an order check. It does not set a millimetre scale.

calibrationProposal.note: After the worn fronts exist and the owner has approved the overlays, submit six raw cards: TD-01 and Karros (sharp on all four corners), TD-02 (a fitted radius on one orientation), and three worn cards that carry a soft corner, a ding, and fraying. The first six stay with those white-border and worn cards. Foil, the halftone Pokémon card, and the full-bleed card wait. If the six corner subgrades fall on one half-point, stop.

phone: A phone corner is not scored. It waits until those two edges already match the centering key, on a still in the ±0.1 mm tier (at or above 30 px/mm) or the ±0.2 mm tier (from 15 px/mm up to 30).
